name: Park Hyatt London River Thames
positioning: Contemporary, art-filled Park Hyatt beside the River Thames in London's Nine Elms district
best_for: Travelers who want river or city views from floor-to-ceiling windows
Guests interested in art and Cantonese dining
Families who need connected rooms, and guests travelling with dogs

facts.text: The hotel is at 7 Nine Elms Lane, London SW8 5PH.
The hotel is close to Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, Tate Britain, Battersea Park, Sloane Square and the King's Road.
The spa has six treatment rooms and a riverside relaxation room with two Somadome Pods and sauna facilities.
Guests can use an indoor heated pool and a double-height fitness centre.
Wellness facilities occupy a dedicated floor with natural daylight.
Yu Ge is the hotel's Cantonese restaurant, led by Head Chef Eng Soon Yeo.
The Nine Elms Kitchen focuses on British produce prepared in an open kitchen, with a dining room and terrace.
The Nine Elms Bar serves classic and inventive cocktails with small bites.
All guest rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows with city or river views.
The Family Room combines an accessible king room with a twin-bed room.

highlights.text: The lobby features a Charlie Whinney commission, Ebb and Flow, and Ian Rayer-Smith's Land and Water painting, both paying homage to the River Thames.
Yu Ge is a riverside Cantonese restaurant inspired by imperial traditions from the Song dynasty.
The corner river-view rooms open onto a 90-degree view of the River Thames.
Corner rooms have a wardrobe with William Morris wallpaper, reachable from both the bedroom and the bathroom.
Work by 20 artists runs through the hotel's spaces.

considerations.text: The hotel sits in Nine Elms, described as a residential district of London.
Valet parking is offered, subject to availability.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
